the intra- and interindividual biological variation of CA 15. 3 and CEA is low, that the indices of individuality of these tumor markers are low, that the variation during breast monitoring is dominated by the biological variation, that the analytical imprecision is low, that CVP and CVI are the main contributors to the variation in tumor marker concentrations, that the indices are useful for evaluating the clinical usefulness of tumor markers, and that conventional cutoff limits should not be applied in breast cancer monitoring

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results for the tumor markers CA 15. 3, CEA, and TPA during breast cancer monitoring are influenced by both intra- and inter- individual biological variation as well as by analytical imprecision.
a change in the level of CA 15. 3, CEA, or TPA is not necessarily an indication of tumor recurrence.
the results of the tumor markers are not useful for the initial detection of breast cancer, but that the results of CA 15. 3, CEA, and TPA are useful for monitoring the course of breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the biological variation of CA 15. 3, CEA, and TPA is high in healthy women and that analytical imprecision is an important component of the variation in breast cancer patients.
CA 15. 3, CEA, and TPA have limited value for monitoring breast cancer.
the biological variation of the tumor markers is so large that it is impossible to identify breast cancer patients on the basis of a single measurement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the variation of CA 15. 3, CEA, and TPA during breast cancer monitoring is considerable and that the use of a conventional cutoff limit is inappropriate.
the biological variation should always be considered in the interpretation of tumor marker results.
the biological variation and analytical imprecision of tumor markers should be considered when evaluating their clinical performance.
